desc:
Entity: Technology Job Family Group: IT&S Group Job Description: About the team The Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team is bp Upstream’s embedded delivery capability. We forward-deploy AI-enabled data scientists and engineers directly into an operating region, working shoulder-to-shoulder with the business to solve real problems in days, not quarters — and to validate the value before investment is committed. Each team member owns solutions end-to-end (the person who frames the problem is the person who ships and sustains it), builds deep domain knowledge in-region, and works alongside AI tooling to punch far beyond the weight of a small team. It is a federated model: centrally governed, locally executed, and AI-enabled by design. The role As a Data Scientist in the FDE team, you are embedded with one of bp’s Upstream operating regions, working alongside experienced data scientists and business customers to build and deliver data science and AI solutions to real operational problems. You’ll take ownership of well-defined pieces of work — from exploring live data and building models through to helping users adopt what you’ve built — and grow quickly into owning solutions end-to-end. With AI tooling, the Foundry Fellowship and hands-on coaching behind you, this is a role for someone who wants to learn fast, ship real things and see their work make a difference. Put simply, your job is to help turn data into decisions. This is a fresh graduate opportunity for Omani nationals looking to start their career in data science and AI. What you’ll do Work with business customers and senior team members in-region to understand operational problems and translate them into clear, data-driven questions. Explore, clean and prepare live operational data, and build analyses, models and proofs-of-concept that answer those questions. Apply data science, machine learning and AI techniques to deliver measurable outcomes — cost reduced, hours freed, safety improved, production protected. Take ownership of defined workstreams within a solution, with increasing autonomy, through development, iteration and adoption. Use AI tooling as a “virtual team member” to accelerate build and learning, compressing development time. Support business users to adopt solutions, explaining results clearly and capturing feedback to improve what we build. Follow good engineering, data science and AI governance practice, keeping work secure, well-documented and easy to hand over. What you’ll bring (essential) Hands-on experience in data science, machine learning or analytics (including internships, placements, graduate schemes or relevant postgraduate research). A degree in a quantitative field (e.g. computer science, statistics, mathematics, engineering, physics) or equivalent practical experience. Solid programming skills in Python (and/or R) and SQL, with experience building models and working with real-world data. A grounding in core statistics and machine learning methods, and the curiosity to apply them to messy, practical problems. The ability to communicate findings clearly to non-technical audiences and work collaboratively with business stakeholders. A customer-centric, pragmatic mindset with a bias for delivering value and a willingness to take ownership. A strong learning mindset — open to feedback, comfortable with ambiguity and keen to use AI tooling to accelerate delivery. Nice to have Experience with Palantir Foundry (Ontology, AIP) — helpful, but this will be built in role through the Foundry Fellowship and on-the-job coaching. Experience with AI-assisted coding tools (e.g. Claude Code, Copilot). Exposure to cloud platforms, version control and basic MLOps / productionisation practice. Interest in, or exposure to, operational Upstream domains (production, operations, maintenance & reliability, wells, subsurface or procurement). Experience energy industry is nice to have. Why join us You’ll learn by doing — embedded with the business, working on real problems with real users, and supported by experienced data scientists who’ll coach you as you grow. With AI tooling, the Foundry Fellowship and a supportive central team behind you, you’ll build your capability fast, take on more ownership quickly and see the value of your work land with the people who use it. title: Data Scientist
desc:
WHY FACULTY? 


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here https://faculty.ai/impact.



We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.



Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.



AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the role:

As a Data Scientist, you will work closely with clients and cross functional teams to define project scope, ensure technical feasibility, and drive delivery excellence.

You’ll design and deliver bespoke data science solutions, shaping the technical direction of high-impact projects and solidifying our reputation as a leader in practical, measurable AI. 



What you'll be doing:

 - Mapping the end-to-end data science approach and designing the associated software architecture for projects

 - Driving the technical scoping and feasibility assessment of new projects

 - Building strong client relationships by acting as a technical advisor and shaping the direction of current and future engagements

 - Delivering bespoke algorithms and scalable software solutions that adhere to best practices for high-stakes decision-making

 - Setting the technical bar for the project team, ensuring the highest standards of code, rigour, and delivery quality (IC leadership)

 - Contributing to Faculty's thought leadership and reputation through teaching, public speaking, or open-source projects



Who we're looking for:

 - You have proven experience in a professional data science or quantitative academic role, underpinned by high mathematical and statistical competence.

 - You are a strong Python programmer, proficient in essential libraries (NumPy, Pandas) and a deep-learning framework (TensorFlow/PyTorch).

 - You possess a solid grasp of core data science techniques (supervised/unsupervised learning, time-series, NLP, model validation) and the ability to innovate new algorithms.

 - You apply a rigorous scientific and entrepreneurial mindset, translating complex business problems into a mathematical framework and measuring model impact upon deployment.

 - You are an exceptional communicator, adept at translating complex technical solutions into persuasive, actionable insights for senior and non-technical audiences.

 - You contribute to team success by project planning, assessing technical feasibility, estimating delivery timelines, and achieving measurable outcomes.



Our Interview Process

Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

Take Home Technical Assessment 

Technical Interview (90 minutes) 

Commercial Interview (60 minutes)

 




OUR RECRUITMENT ETHOS




We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.



If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. 



A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.
